army_chief_of_artillery.name: Brigadier General Henry Hunt
army_chief_of_artillery.notes: Hunt managed ammunition supply before Pickett's Charge -- deliberately silenced Union guns over Hancock's objections to conserve rounds. His decision is credited with allowing Union artillery to devastate Confederate infantry during the charge itself.

metadata.notes: A 6-gun battery online occupies roughly 42 yards of front. Total Union guns approximately 370 including horse artillery.

commander.name: Lieutenant Colonel Freeman McGilvery
commander.notes: McGilvery's emergency construction of the Plum Run Line on July 2 evening -- assembling guns from multiple batteries to plug the gap left by Sickles' collapse -- is one of the finest improvised artillery actions of the war.

batteries.key_action: McGilvery's Line July 2 evening -- helped stop Confederate advance. Fought during Pickett's Charge July 3.

Fighting withdrawal from Trostle Farm July 2 -- ordered to hold without support to buy time for McGilvery to form the Plum Run line. Lost 28 men and several guns but accomplished the mission. One of the most celebrated artillery actions of the battle.
batteries.flag_notes: CRITICAL ANIMATION: withdrawal from Trostle Farm lane -- battery limbering under fire, moving by sections, losing a gun, final stand at the Trostle Farm wall. Multiple disposition changes across 4-5 ticks.

commander.name: Colonel Charles Wainwright
commander.notes: Wainwright kept a superb diary -- one of the best artillery primary sources for Gettysburg.

batteries.flag_notes: Hall's Battery is featured in a Gettysburg Animated YouTube vignette. Must be placed with high precision at McPherson's Ridge and Railroad Cut area.

commander.name: Lieutenant T. Fred Brown
commander.fate: Wounded July 3 -- severely wounded in Confederate cannonade

batteries.key_action: Cemetery Ridge -- opposite The Angle during Pickett's Charge. Brown severely wounded in the cannonade.
Second Corps artillery -- Cemetery Ridge July 2-3.

commander.name: Lieutenant George Woodruff
commander.fate: KIA July 3 -- killed during Pickett's Charge

batteries.key_action: Cemetery Ridge -- Woodruff killed during Pickett's Charge. Guns fired canister into Pettigrew's and Trimble's advancing Confederates.

commander.name: Lieutenant Alonzo Cushing
commander.fate: KIA July 3 -- killed at The Angle while serving his last gun. Received Medal of Honor posthumously 2014 -- longest gap between action and award in MOH history.

batteries.key_action: The Angle -- Cushing's battery stood directly opposite the Confederate breakthrough. As Armistead's men surged over the wall Cushing rolled his last two guns to the wall and was killed serving them.
batteries.flag_notes: HIGHEST PRIORITY PLACEMENT: Cushing's battery must be positioned immediately behind The Angle stone wall. Precision required to within 20 meters.

batteries.key_action: Second Corps artillery -- Cemetery Ridge.
Third Corps -- Peach Orchard salient July 2.
Peach Orchard -- heavily engaged. 19 casualties.
Wheatfield area -- one of the most contested artillery positions of Day 2.
Devil's Den -- one of the most famous artillery positions of the battle. Guns briefly captured by Hood's Confederates then recaptured.
batteries.flag_notes: Devil's Den gun position -- must be placed precisely among the boulders. Among the most photographed positions on the battlefield.

commander.name: Lieutenant Charles Hazlett
commander.fate: KIA July 2 -- shot on Little Round Top summit beside the dying Weed

batteries.key_action: Hazlett's battery dragged its guns up the steep rocky slope of Little Round Top. Technically too elevated to fire effectively on Confederate infantry below but their moral effect was significant. Hazlett killed beside Weed -- both dying on the summit at nearly the same moment.
batteries.flag_notes: Little Round Top summit -- guns placed at rocky peak. Hazlett and Weed killed together is a vignette-worthy simultaneous event.

commander.name: Major Thomas Osborn
commander.notes: Osborn organized the massed artillery on Cemetery Hill that played a critical defensive role.

commander.name: Captain Hubert Dilger
commander.fate: Survived -- Medal of Honor for Gettysburg
commander.notes: 'Leatherbreeches' Dilger was born in Germany, served in European armies. MOH for delaying Rodes's attack at close range while Union infantry retreated through Gettysburg.

batteries.key_action: Fought in the most dramatic artillery action of July 1 -- engaged Confederate infantry at close range IN THE STREETS OF GETTYSBURG to cover the Union retreat. Fighting withdrawal through the town itself.
batteries.flag_notes: UNIQUE PLACEMENT: Dilger's battery moved THROUGH Gettysburg's streets during the retreat -- the only artillery unit to fight in the town. Requires precise in-town placement across several ticks.

batteries.key_action: XI Corps -- north of town July 1 then Cemetery Hill.

commander.name: Lieutenant Bayard Wilkeson
commander.fate: KIA July 1 -- both legs shattered; reportedly amputated one leg himself with a penknife before dying

batteries.key_action: Barlow's Knoll July 1 -- most exposed Union artillery position. Wilkeson had both legs shattered. He reportedly amputated one leg himself with a penknife and bled to death.
batteries.flag_notes: Barlow's Knoll -- most exposed Union position July 1. Wilkeson's mortal wounding is one of the most harrowing stories of Day 1.
